newsitem.title: USA: Alberta plans to double oil drilling in 97.
newsitem.headline: Alberta plans to double oil drilling in 97.

text.p: Alberta Energy Co plans to more than double its drilling activity and increase capital expenditure by a third next year, a company executive said Thursday.

"We'll have 600 net wells in 1997...and capital expenditures will reach $600 million," up from $450 million this year, said Brian Moss, vice president of new ventures at AEC West, one of Alberta Energy's three main subsidiaries.

AEC drilled a company record 231 exploration and development wells in the first half of the year. Active wells this year stood at 290, Moss said, and next year's planned increase to 600 wells will consist of 200 exploratory and 400 producing wells.

He forecast that total liquids production, including syncrude, would be 65,000 barrels a day in 1997 compared with 61,000 in 1996. Excluding syncrude, a crude extracted from oilsand and shale, Alberta's liquids output should rise to 37,000 from 31,000 bpd this year.
Moss spoke to Reuters while attending the Herold energy conference in Greenwich, Connecticut.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620
